tagline: Names on the cliff, wheel marks in the rock.
intro: From the Nebraska line, US 26 runs west through Torrington, Lingle, Fort Laramie and Guernsey to Interstate 25. Near the state line a marker shows where the Oregon Trail itself entered Wyoming. At Torrington, the old Union Pacific depot now houses the Homesteaders Museum.

Near Guernsey, the older traffic left records without paper. Emigrants cut their names into Register Cliff, a sandstone face rising a hundred feet above the North Platte valley, while wagon wheels and draft animals wore the nearby trail into rock, in places several feet deep.

moments.title: Torrington
moments.text: The preserved Union Pacific depot houses the Homesteaders Museum, putting the homesteading years inside a building made for travel.

moments.title: Fort Laramie
moments.text: Twenty-two original structures remain at the post that began in the fur trade, became an army fort and served as a stop for emigrant wagon trains.

moments.title: Oregon Trail Ruts
moments.text: Wheels and draft animals wore the trail two to six feet into a sandstone ridge, on a line chosen to avoid the marshy ground beside the river.
